title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
gist: Qwik 2.0 RC (Oct 1, 2026) replaces v1's HTML comment markers with end-of-document qwik/state and qwik/vnode script blocks, enabling experimental out-of-order streaming; self-reported benchmarks put v2 at 1.23x vanilla JS (vs v1 2.59x, React 19 1.53x) and pre-interactivity JS fell from 59KB to 9KB in one walkthrough. It landed the same day as SvelteKit 3 and Remix 3.0.

insights.claim: Qwik, the resumable JavaScript framework originally created at Builder.io, published its 2.0 Release Candidate as @qwik.dev/core@2.0.0-rc.0 on 1 October 2026, about two years and eight months after the initial 'Towards Qwik 2.0' design article.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The long v2 cycle signals slow execution for a niche framework; watch whether the RC converts to a stable release and adoption.

insights.claim: Qwik v1 used HTML comment markers like <!--qv--> throughout rendered HTML to flag component boundaries, which forced a single ordered write pass, added CPU and memory overhead, and made out-of-order streaming impossible because a slow fetch blocked everything after it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Explains the architectural debt v2 removes; serialization format choices directly cap streaming and SSR performance in web frameworks.
insights.quote: That approach forced a single ordered write pass, added CPU and memory overhead, and made out-of-order streaming impossible
insights.locator: In v1, Qwik propagated state updates

insights.claim: Qwik v2 eliminates HTML comment markers and instead compresses state and virtual node information into two script blocks (qwik/state and qwik/vnode) at the end of the document.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Moving serialized state to end-of-document enables streaming and lighter HTML, a pattern other resumable/SSR frameworks may follow.
insights.locator: In v1, Qwik propagated state updates

insights.claim: On Qwik's internal js-framework-benchmark runs, Qwik v2 scores a weighted geometric mean 1.23x slower than vanilla JavaScript, ahead of Vue 3.5 (1.25x), Angular 22 (1.42x), React 19 with the compiler (1.53x) and Qwik v1 (2.59x).
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Vendor-run benchmark claims v2 roughly doubles v1 speed and edges out major frameworks; treat as self-reported until independently replicated.
insights.locator: On Qwik's internal runs of js-framework-benchmark

insights.claim: A Classmethod walkthrough building the same starter on Qwik v1 and v2 found server-rendered HTML comments fell from 60 to zero and JavaScript required before interactivity dropped from 59KB to 9KB, although total bundle size grew.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Trade-off: much less upfront JS for interactivity at the cost of larger total bundles; relevant to performance-sensitive web teams evaluating frameworks.
insights.quote: JavaScript required before interactivity dropping from 59KB to 9KB, though total bundle size grew

insights.claim: Qwik 2.0 adds experimental out-of-order HTML streaming: developers wrap slow regions in <Pending> and <Catch> boundaries so the server sends the rest of the page immediately and streams real content later in the same response, opted into via vite.config.ts experimental flags.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Closes a known feature gap versus competitors; experimental status means production adoption likely lags.
insights.locator: Out-of-order HTML streaming has also been added

insights.claim: Qwik 2.0 lets useComputed$ accept async functions (replacing <Resource>) and gives route loaders their own JSON endpoints with cacheControl and eTag options so browsers can cache them individually and <Link> can prefetch data on hover.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Per-loader HTTP caching and hover prefetch push data-loading performance toward CDN-friendly patterns.

insights.claim: Qwik 2.0 adds a worker$ primitive for Web Workers, reactify$ for embedding Qwik components inside React trees, server-only *.server.ts files, and HMR that preserves signal and store values across edits.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: reactify$ offers an incremental adoption path inside React codebases, the main lever for a minority framework to gain share.
insights.locator: Other additions include a worker$ primitive

insights.claim: Before the v2 RC, a Reddit developer called Qwik's lack of out-of-order streaming a significant limitation and argued the team should be more upfront about it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Shows streaming was a real adoption blocker that v2 is designed to address.
insights.locator: In a Reddit discussion predating the v2 RC

insights.claim: Qwik v2 had a long gestation, reaching alpha in November 2024 and beta in June 2025, while v1 kept receiving updates through version 1.20.1 in September 2026, per Hiroshi Morishige of Classmethod.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Parallel maintenance of v1 and v2 stretches a small team; release cadence is a proxy for project health.
insights.locator: In his Classmethod walkthrough, Hiroshi Morishige

insights.claim: SvelteKit 3 and Remix 3.0 shipped stable releases on the same day as the Qwik 2.0 RC, all three within seven hours; Qwik 2 and SvelteKit 3 use Vite 8 while Remix 3 is independent of Vite.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Vite's consolidation as the default build layer across frameworks strengthens its ecosystem position; Remix is the notable outlier.
insights.quote: Qwik 2 and SvelteKit 3 use Vite 8; Remix 3 is independent of Vite.
insights.locator: He also noted that SvelteKit 3 and Remix 3.0

insights.claim: The Qwik team says v2 breaking changes are small and automated by 'pnpm qwik migrate-v2', which also migrates to the new @qwik.dev/core and @qwik.dev/router package names; Qwik remains MIT-licensed and developed on GitHub.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Low migration friction and the package rename suggest a move toward an independent project identity.
insights.locator: The team says the breaking changes are small
